title: No release for v2.2.0
body:
Although Pypi reports 2.2.0 being available, there is no corresponding tag on the git repository.
Could you please create one ?

Context: updating triton in the nixpkgs repository.

Thanks !

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> There is a branch.

Thank you for the hint.
Would it still be feasible to create a tag for this release ?
We tend to directly fetch packages upstream sources from the git repositories using a release tag.

Thank you for your help and consideration.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@reporter 

> Would it still be feasible to create a tag for this release ?

JFYI: the tag is not likely to help here, since the commit history for the release branches (including `release/2.2.x`) appears to have been modified retroactively, which broke the build (see issue #3525).

In particular, the commit [you have](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/292996/files#diff-12d5872269fe05b4b44d02433ddaf5804f72b72ccda1c3b488d50684ba3cf889R44) for the 2.2 release in the nixpkgs PR is [no longer part of this repository](https://github.com/openai/triton/commit/0e7b97bd47fc4beb21ae960a516cd9a7ae9bc060):

![image](https://github.com/openai/triton/assets/42850/d330dff2-9707-41f2-b12b-39f1d16291be)

The replacement commit is [0149bf70042efb998fc7a1ea30ed99e3a0f75053](https://github.com/openai/triton/commit/0149bf70042efb998fc7a1ea30ed99e3a0f75053), which is affected by issue #3525 as well.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Ok this makes sense.
Thank you for this explanation !
Feel free to close this issue then.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> Feel free to close this issue then.

Uh, sorry, I worded that confusingly. :/ Having a `v2.2.0` tag would be very valuable, exactly because it's supposed to be immutable (as opposed to a release branch). All I was saying was that, as of right now, there is no valid commit that can be tagged with `v2.2.0`. Hopefully the situation in issue #3525 will be resolved somehow, and then a tag can be made.

(and just to clarify, I'm not a Triton developer/contributor, so all of the above is just my personal opinion)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Got it !

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
We definitely should not be modifying history on the release branch, yikes.  I'll raise this with Phil; maybe the release branch is not protected from force pushes.

WRT making a tag, I'll ask the folks who maintain the release branch.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @participant11 how would you feel about making release tags?  Given that we messed up and force-pushed to the release branch, it sort of feels like we ought to make proper tags so they're immutable.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Yes, I am very sorry for screwing things up over the weekend. I think it can be reverted though!

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: the history of the release branch should be back to normal now. Can you confirm that it works? Sorry again for the disruption.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> Can you confirm that it works?

It does, thank you! I just closed issue #3525.

Regarding this issue: given that the branch history is restored, I think it is now possible to tag 0e7b97bd47fc4beb21ae960a516cd9a7ae9bc060 (the original untagged commit used in the draft nixpkgs PR and the current `HEAD` of `release/2.2.x`) as `v2.2.0`, and call it a day?

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: This is a very confusing thread to follow. So what it is the exact commit for triton 2.2.0 released to pip? tip of https://github.com/openai/triton/tree/release/2.2.x  or a commit on the branch but not the tip? Thanks.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: It would also be great to get a tag for v2.3.0 at the same time. Currently there's a release branch - however, I was wondering whether it would be possible to please tag the commit relating to the pypi release? This is to support the CUDA variant of PyTorch in Anaconda's main channel - i.e., to distribute v2.3.0 of Triton as a conda package. I can see the [commit used by PyTorch](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/v2.3.0-rc12/.ci/docker/ci_commit_pins/triton.txt) for their release, however, this seems to [not be on a branch any more](https://github.com/openai/triton/commit/79c6c9b209a5692b9a895398f4f3a033f8f80415). A tagged commit would be preferable from a SHA (even though a SHA is less mutable, we still should be able to claim that we're releasing a certain upstream version)

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: Ideally, a proper github source release would be best

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hello,
Could the 2.2.0 tag been made please ? It would allow to close this issue and for us to package it correctly.

Thank you very much !

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: The 2.3.0 one as well please 🙏

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
+1 to tagging releases please - many downstream ecosystems depend on tags for automated updates - like conda-forge.

Without them, maintainers don't get notified that new upstream releases are available.

https://github.com/conda-forge/triton-feedstock

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant1 sorry to bother you with this issue but this prevents us (nixpkgs maintainers, and apparently conda's too) from shipping the latest triton updates to our users.

Thank you very much for your consideration
